speaker: NARRATOR
text: [darker, lower] Now. Think about who loves the idea that heart disease comes from your personality... and your stress.

speaker: AD VOICE
text: [bright, polished, too smooth] Tense? Wound up? Long day at the office? [beat] Take a moment. Light up. Relax.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Decades later, researchers dug through millions of pages of tobacco industry documents. And they found something.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: In 1958, Hans Selye, the father of stress, wrote to a tobacco company asking for money.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: He got it. A lot of it. Over the years, the industry funded his work, and it used stress research in court, to argue that something else was making people sick.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: He didn't publicly declare those ties.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: And Type A? A later study found the tobacco industry had been a major funder of that research too.

speaker: YOU
text: [quiet, stunned] ...So the cigarette companies helped sell me my stress.

speaker: AD VOICE
text: [distant, fading, like a memory] ...Light up. Relax.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [gently] They helped sell you a story about it. That stress is a thing that happens to you. A thing that breaks you. And that you need something to take the edge off.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [pause] And that story might be doing more harm than the stress itself.
